faq: Will existing users notice a broken experience?
No. We change the look and layout, not the stored data or core logic. We test the old and new versions side by side so every saved setting still shows up in the new screens.
Do I need to give you my designs?
Not at all. You can share brand colors, a logo and any apps you like for reference, and we propose the layout. If you already have designs, we build from them.
Can you redesign without the source code?
We need the source files to rebuild the interface properly. If you only have the published package, we can often unpack it, but we confirm what is possible before quoting.
Will the redesign change my permissions?
No. A visual refresh does not need new permissions, so users are not shown a fresh warning and the update goes through the normal review.
desc:
Browser extension UI redesign from Ecom Swift LLC gives your existing extension a clearer, modern interface across its popup, settings and panels, while the working logic and your users' saved data stay safe.

## What does a browser extension UI redesign cover?

A browser extension UI redesign changes how the extension looks and feels without changing what it does. It covers the popup that opens from the toolbar, the options page, any side panel and the small details: icons, colors, spacing, text size, button labels and the messages shown when something is empty or goes wrong.

The code underneath keeps running. The aim is that a person who used the old version recognizes the tool, and a new person understands it faster.

## Why interface quality changes how people judge your extension

People judge an extension in a few seconds, and often from a screenshot on the store page. A cramped popup, mixed fonts and unclear buttons suggest a tool that is not looked after, even if the code is excellent. Users hesitate to trust it with their pages or their data.

A clear interface does practical work. It shows the main action first, groups related settings and explains errors in words a non-technical person understands. That reduces support questions, helps new users reach their first success and gives the store screenshots something worth looking at.

## What a strong redesign includes

- A review of the current screens, with notes on what confuses people.
- Layout sketches for your approval before any code changes.
- A consistent set of colors, type sizes and spacing across every screen.
- A new icon set, in the sizes the browsers use.
- Clear button labels and short, plain help text.
- Designed empty, loading and error states.
- Light and dark themes where the package includes them.
- Controls that work with a keyboard and show a visible focus mark.
- Text and background contrast readable at small sizes.
- New store screenshots that match the new look.

## How we carry out the work

We start with your current extension and a conversation about what bothers you and your users. Then we sketch the new layout for each screen and send it for approval. After that we rebuild the interface in the code, connect it to your existing logic and test every action to be sure nothing moved out of reach.

The Basic, Standard and Premium packages differ in scope. Basic refreshes one popup with new icons and colors. Standard redesigns up to three screens, rebuilds the settings page and adds light and dark themes with designed empty and error states. Premium extends to a full refresh with a side panel layout, small motion on key actions, a one-page style guide and a keyboard and screen reader pass.

Existing users keep their saved data. We test upgrades from the old version before anything is released.

## Do and avoid in an interface refresh

**Do:**
- Keep the main action visible without scrolling.
- Use one type scale and one spacing scale throughout.
- Test at the real size of the popup, not a large preview.
- Keep familiar controls where users expect them.
- Show what has been saved after a setting changes.

**Avoid:**
- Moving every control at once and confusing loyal users.
- Using tiny gray text on a white background.
- Adding animation that delays the main task.
- Relying on color alone to show an error.
- Redesigning the store screenshots before the interface is final.

## Who this is for

It suits an owner whose extension works well but looks dated beside newer competitors. It suits a company rebranding its products that needs its extension to match. And it suits a developer who built a useful tool and wants a designer's eye on the screens.

## What we need from you

Send the source code or a build, any brand files such as a logo and colors, and a note on what you dislike about the current look. If you have designs, share them, though you do not need to have any.

We never ask for passwords. You can invite us to your repository or send a zip file. If we do work without the code, we can still produce designs and screenshots, and your developer applies them. After you order, we reply with the first questions and a sketch plan.
